findings.detail: scored 0 — The answer correctly states the subsample qualifier requirement for turbidity/temperature/DO/Eh but it refuses the flow-cell sampling question and omits the storage limits and time-sensitivity guidance withholding facts the rubric expects a real answer for. Unmet: States plainly that a discrete turbidity sample must not be collected from the discharge passing through the flow-through chamber holding the other sensors; Gives the storage limits if the sample cannot be read on site: clean amber bottle out of sunlight chilled at or below 4 C held no longer than 24 hours; Notes turbidity is time sensitive and should be measured on site preferably in situ

scored 0 — The answer makes none of the must-contain points and instead treats the two tables as a possible conflict resolving it by advising to apply whichever set is stricter rather than stating they agree. Unmet: States plainly that the two tables give the same stabilisation criteria and do not conflict; States the general field-measurement chapter itself points multiparameter users to the multiparameter chapter for criteria of the same kind; States the criteria are standard sensor stabilisation criteria and that actual sensor accuracy varies by model and manufacturer a separate matter; For persistent variability extends equilibration and records additional measurements then reports the median of the final five or more readings or selects a representative final reading with documented judgment

scored 0 — The answer refuses the A6.8 field-form criteria entirely so none of the three must-contain points (the ±0.1 unit criterion the ±0.3 unit below 75 µS/cm criterion and the distinction from A6.4's 0.05-unit final-buffer check) are made though it correctly states A6.4's check and violates no must-not item. Unmet: Attributes ±0.1 pH unit to the A6.8 example field form's calibration criterion; Attributes ±0.3 pH unit below 75 µS/cm to that example form; Distinguishes the form's conductivity-dependent criteria from A6.4's final-buffer check requiring agreement within 0.05 pH unit of the certified value at calibration temperature

scored 0 — The answer is a refusal that supplies none of the required values the 0.03 mg/L difference the Benson and Krause note the ±0.2 mg/L tolerance comparison or the advice to use one protocol's table consistently. Unmet: gives the USGS table value at 20.0 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.09 mg/L; gives the EPA chart value at 20 C and 760 mmHg as about 9.06 mg/L; states the difference is 0.03 mg/L and assesses its significance against the applicable procedure; notes the USGS values are generated from the Benson and Krause equations; compares the 0.03 mg/L difference with the USGS saturation-check tolerance of ±0.2 mg/L; advises using the table belonging to whichever protocol the work is being done under consistently

scored 0 — The answer gives the multiplication method and cites table 6.2–4 but withholds the required factor 0.8235 saying it cannot give the specific factor which is a refusal of a figure the rubric expects. Unmet: Gives 0.8235 as the factor for 20.0 °C at 50 000 µS/cm

scored 0 — The answer places pH before specific conductance violating a must-not item and omits the temperature-first sequence the lower-to-higher ionic-strength rationale and the pH-buffer contamination note. Unmet: Places temperature first in the sequence; Places specific conductance before pH; Places dissolved oxygen and then oxidation-reduction potential after pH; Explains that the sequence runs from lower to higher ionic strength so carryover from one standard does not bias the next; Notes specifically that pH buffers and electrode filling solutions are high in ionic strength and would contaminate a conductivity calibration
